children: Our Bureau New Delhi: Automobile sales in India climbed 20% to 30 million units in the 11 months since the government cut goods and services tax (GST) last September. The move boosted affordability across categories as automakers dropped prices in line with the reduced tax rates, helping draw first-time buyers to showrooms in both urban and rural markets, said industry executives.

At Maruti Suzuki, passenger vehicle sales surged nearly 36% from a year earlier in the April-August period, with the entry-level segment expanding more than 96%. "This demonstrates the power of the Indian consumer and the importance of affordability," said Hisashi Takeuchi, managing director & CEO, Maruti Suzuki, adding that the company is accelerating capex plans, with a "multiplier effect across the economy" expected to follow.

Hyundai Motor India echoed the trend. "The GST 2.0 reforms have been a significant catalyst for the Indian automotive industry," said Tarun Garg, MD & CEO, HMIL, noting that monthly wholesale volumes of over 400,000 units have become "the new normal." Passenger vehicle industry sales grew over 15% y-o-y between September 2025 and March 2026, accelerating to more than 29% in the subsequent five months, Garg said.

Indian auto retail has registered over 30 million vehicles, growing nearly 20% year-on-year, against under 5% in the comparable year before the reform, Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations data showed. FADA president Sai Giridhar said two-wheeler sales have hit levels last seen in 2018, alternative-fuel vehicles have overtaken petrol models in the passenger segment for the first time, and rural markets are now outpacing urban ones.

Improved affordability, he said, "did not merely pull demand forward; it widened the market itself." The impact has extended well beyond passenger vehicles. Anish Shah, Group CEO & MD, Mahindra Group, said SUV sales have grown 17% since the rationalisation, while light commercial vehicles and tractors have risen 20%.

He added that the reform has lifted disbursements at Mahindra Finance and boosted discretionary spending across the group's hospitality, real estate and logistics businesses. "GST 2.0 demonstrates how structural reforms, when combined with strong consumer demand and business investment, can create a virtuous cycle of affordability, consumption, investment and growth," Shah said.

title: Auto Retail Sales Rise 20% as GST Cut Boosts Affordability
